card: Enables SQLite secure_delete by default when opening wallet databases and in the SQLite depends package, ensuring deleted or overwritten data is zeroed out on disk. Rotating a wallet passphrase previously left superseded master key records lingering in SQLite database free space, because explicit purging via VACUUM only occurred on initial encryption. The change eliminates WalletDatabase::Rewrite and adds functional tests verifying that unencrypted keys and rotated master keys do not remain in the raw database file.
changed_since_previous: Functional tests were added to wallet_encryption.py to verify that unencrypted private keys and rotated master keys are erased from the wallet file.
evidence: PR description: 'l0rinc's LLMs recently found changing the passphrase can leave the original that encryption key record in free pages. We should want to ensure that those records are also deleted...'

PR description: 'Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, and NixOS all set SQLite's compile time option to default secure_delete to enabled... This suggests to me that the performance penalty is not actually that bad.'
problem: Sensitive wallet records can persist in unallocated database pages after updates or deletions. While initial wallet encryption previously called VACUUM to purge unencrypted keys, passphrase changes (rotating the master encryption key) and regular deletions left overwritten records intact in SQLite free pages.

risk.why: Alters low-level SQLite database write behavior and relies on secure_delete in place of explicit VACUUM on initial encryption; an issue could cause database corruption or degrade wallet I/O performance.

summary: Enables SQLite's secure_delete PRAGMA by default for wallet databases and sets -DSQLITE_SECURE_DELETE in the SQLite depends build. This causes SQLite to zero out deleted or overwritten content instead of leaving records in free pages. The change removes WalletDatabase::Rewrite, which previously ran an explicit VACUUM only during initial wallet encryption, and adds functional tests verifying key erasure.
